title: Another Day Its Course Hath Run
description: Another Day Its Course Hath Run in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Pierpont wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 372, “Evening Hymn for a Child”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: An-oth-er day its course hath run, And still, O God! Thy child is blest; For Thou hast been by day my sun, And Thou wilt be by night my rest.

lines: Another day its course hath run,
And still, O God! Thy child is blest;
For Thou hast been by day my sun,
And Thou wilt be by night my rest.
Sweet sleep descends, mine eyes to close;
And now, while all the world is still,
I give my body to repose,
My spirit to my Father's will.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Pierpont died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Pierpont (1785–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
